title: An octopus has 3 hearts?!

scenes.narration_display: Did you know one animal has three hearts?
scenes.narration_tts: Did you know one animal has three hearts?
scenes.visual_description: A glowing question mark and a big glossy red cartoon heart float over a deep-blue gradient stage, sparkles drifting around them.

scenes.narration_display: Meet the octopus, a clever sea animal! It does not have one heart. It has three!
scenes.narration_tts: Meet the octopus, a clever sea animal! It does not have one heart. It has three!
scenes.visual_description: A friendly purple cartoon octopus with big shiny eyes waves its eight curly arms on a sunny coral reef, bubbles rising.

scenes.narration_display: Two small hearts push blood through its gills. The third heart sends blood to the rest of its body.
scenes.narration_tts: Two small hearts push blood through its gills. The third heart sends blood to the rest of its body.
scenes.visual_description: Inside a translucent cartoon octopus, three glowing hearts pulse: two small ones beside the gills and one bigger one in the middle, soft x-ray style.

scenes.narration_display: Now here is the surprise. When the octopus swims, that third heart stops beating!
scenes.narration_tts: Now here is the surprise. When the octopus swims, that third heart stops beating!
scenes.visual_description: The cartoon octopus starts swimming with a jet of water; its big central heart dims and stops glowing while the two small hearts keep pulsing.

scenes.narration_display: So swimming makes it tired very fast. That is why an octopus likes to crawl instead.
scenes.narration_tts: So swimming makes it tired very fast. That is why an octopus likes to crawl instead.
scenes.visual_description: The tired cartoon octopus sighs and happily crawls along the sandy seabed on its arms instead of swimming, seaweed swaying.

scenes.narration_display: Its blood is not red. It is blue! A protein with copper, called hemocyanin, carries the oxygen.
scenes.narration_tts: Its blood is not red. It is blue! A protein with copper, called hemocyanin, carries the oxygen.
scenes.visual_description: Close-up of a glowing blue droplet of blood swirling in a playful cartoon lab, tiny copper-colored molecules sparkling inside it.

scenes.narration_display: An octopus has about 500 million nerve cells. Two-thirds of them are in its arms!
scenes.narration_tts: An octopus has about 500 million nerve cells. Two-thirds of them are in its arms!
scenes.visual_description: The octopus's arms light up with thousands of tiny glowing neurons, most of the sparkle running along the arms, a small glowing brain in the head.

scenes.narration_display: And its suckers can even taste the things they touch.
scenes.narration_tts: And its suckers can even taste the things they touch.
scenes.visual_description: An octopus arm with round suckers touches a seashell; the suckers glow softly as if tasting it, the octopus looks delighted.

scenes.narration_display: Three hearts, blue blood and smart arms. Nature is amazing! Follow for more fun facts.
scenes.narration_tts: Three hearts, blue blood and smart arms. Nature is amazing! Follow for more fun facts.
scenes.visual_description: Celebration on the reef: the octopus, three glowing hearts and confetti bubbles swirl together under bright light shafts.
